key_insight: Platinum photoelectron spectra are shaped by strong many-body losses, satellites, and relativistic spin-orbit effects, which must all be modeled together to correctly interpret Pt electronic structure.
engineering_relevance: The results provide a reliable spectral reference for diagnosing platinum and Pt-based catalysts/materials, improving peak assignment and electronic-structure analysis in XPS and related techniques.
method: RHEELS to map loss features and plasmonic excitations
SXPS and HAXPES to probe shallow and deep core-level satellites
Ab initio DFT and G0W0 calculations, with/without spin-orbit coupling, to interpret valence-band structure
evidence_signal: The study combines multiple spectroscopy datasets with first-principles calculations to assign satellite features, spin-orbit splittings, and valence-band states across metallic Pt.
watch_item: Satellite assignments can depend on energy resolution and model choice, so spectra should be interpreted with careful consideration of instrumental broadening and relativistic effects.
paper_title: Lifetime effects and satellites in the photoelectron spectrum of platinum metal
